(Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) | college = [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] (2000–2001) | draft_year = 2001 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 7 | draft_team = [[New Jersey Nets]] | career_start = 2001 | career_end = 2007 | career_position = [[Power forward]] / [[Center (basketball)|center]] | career_number = 33, 41 | years1 = {{nbay|2001|start}}–{{nbay|2002|end}} | team1 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years2 = {{nbay|2004|start}}–{{nbay|2006|end}} | team2 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] (2002) * [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year]] (2001) * First-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2000) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2000 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2000]]) | stats_league = NBA | stat1label = [[Point (basketball)|Points]] | stat1value = 2,171 (7.2 ppg) | stat2label = [[Rebound (basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = 1,744 (5.8 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 236 (0.8 apg) }} {{wikinews|Former Timberwolf Eddie Griffin dies at 25}} '''Eddie Jamaal Griffin''' (May 30, 1982 – August 17, 2007) was an American professional [[basketball]] player from [[Philadelphia]]. He last played for the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], who waived him on March 13, 2007. Months later, he was killed in a car crash. ==College career== After a standout career at [[Roman Catholic High School]] of [[Philadelphia]] in which he was named ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'s'' National Player of the Year, he competed in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and led Roman to the [[Philadelphia Catholic League]] Championship in his junior and senior years. However, in a harbinger of things to come, Griffin was forced to finish his senior year via correspondence courses after getting in a fight with a teammate.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=adande_ja&page=EddieGriffin|title=Griffin's tragic life a story of talent and temptation|last=Adande|first=J. A.|author-link=J. A. Adande|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=2007-08-22}} As a freshman, Griffin averaged 17.8 points, 10.7 rebounds, and 4.4 blocks for [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] and was at one point thought to be a potential top pick in the [[2001 NBA draft]]. He was named the nation's Freshman of the Year by ''[[Sporting News]]''.{{cite web |url=http://archive.sportingnews.com/cbasketball/awards/freshmanawards.html |title=The Sporting News: Freshman of the Year |work=Sporting News |access-date=2012-01-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090417164449/http://archive.sportingnews.com/cbasketball/awards/freshmanawards.html |archive-date=2009-04-17 }} In January 2001, Griffin got in a fight with teammate Ty Shine. Griffin left the school in somewhat acrimonious circumstances after his freshman year, and made himself available for the NBA Draft.{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/columns/wojnarowski/1142032.html|title=ESPN: Griffin leaves Seton Hall in quandary |work=ESPN.com |date=2001-09-18 |access-date=2020-02-27}} Shortly before the draft, Griffin's half-brother Marvin Powell died of a [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]].{{cite news|last1=Jensen|first1=Mike|title=Eddie Griffin's terrible end|url=http://articles.philly.com/2007-08-26/news/24995483_1_terrible-end-crash-john-lucas|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021044523/http://articles.philly.com/2007-08-26/news/24995483_1_terrible-end-crash-john-lucas|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 21, 2013|access-date=May 31, 2016|work=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=August 26, 2007}}{{cite news|last1=Beck|first1=Howard|title=Comeback Chance for Griffin Ends in Fiery Crash|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/23/sports/basketball/23griffin.html|access-date=May 31, 2016|work=The New York Times|date=August 23, 2007}} ==NBA career== Despite Griffin's freshman year at Seton Hall, the lingering question about his attitude saw him slip to the seventh overall pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]], where he was selected by the [[New Jersey Nets]], who immediately traded the rights to him over to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for those to [[Jason Collins]], [[Brandon Armstrong (basketball)|Brandon Armstrong]], and [[Richard Jefferson]] (all of whom selected likewise in the 2001 draft). In his [[2001–02 NBA season|rookie year]], Griffin played in 73 games (starting 24) while averaging 8.8 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 1.84 blocks per game (ranking 13th in the NBA in that category). He followed this in [[2002–03 NBA season|2002-03]] with per-game averages of 8.6 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 1.44 blocks. Off the court, Griffin suffered from alcoholism, and his troubles piled up quickly over the ensuing year. In December 2003, the Rockets released him after he missed practices and engaged in a team fight. Griffin signed with the Nets in January 2004, only to miss the entire 2003–04 season, when he entered an alcohol rehabilitation center. Prior to the 2004–05 season, the Timberwolves signed Griffin to a one-year contract, for which season he posted roughly the same numbers as he had done for his previous two. The Timberwolves re-signed Griffin for three years (player option in the third), starting with the 2005–06 season. Griffin had a significant drop-off in scoring and rebounding, albeit while suffering only a slight decrease in minutes and while averaging a career-high in blocks per game (2.11). On March 30, 2006, Griffin was involved in a car crash. Witnesses and friends stated that he was watching a "pornographic movie on a DVD in his vehicle, and was masturbating".{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=2505552|title=Tape shows T-Wolves' Griffin saying he was drunk after crash|website=[[ESPN]]|date=June 30, 2006|accessdate=7 January 2024}} After the accident, he proceeded to enter a nearby convenience store, where, as per the store's [[security camera]] footage, he lamented his being drunk and without driver's license to the clerk; it also showed Griffin begging the man whose SUV he had struck not to call the police and promising to buy him a new car in exchange.{{cite web |url=http://wcco.com/topstories/local_story_180133016.html |title=Suit: Wolves Player Watched Porn, Caused Crash |publisher=WCCO |date=2006-06-29 |access-date=2007-03-27 |archive-date=July 3, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060703002653/http://wcco.com/topstories/local_story_180133016.html |url-status=dead }} Griffin's final NBA game was played on December 13, 2006, in an 82–95 Timberwolves loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. Griffin played for 48 seconds and recorded no stats except for a missed three-pointer, his only such attempt of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/griffed01/gamelog/2007|title=Eddie Griffin 2006-07 Game Log|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|accessdate=1 June 2022}} In March 2007, Griffin was released by the Timberwolves.{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves_release_eddie_griffin_070314.html|title=Wolves release Griffin|work=NBA.com|date=March 14, 2007}}{{cite news|first1=Jon|last1=Krawczynski|title=Timberwolves waive F Eddie Griffin|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2007-03-14-3402149529_x.htm|access-date=May 31, 2016|work=USA Today|agency=Associated Press|date=March 14, 2007}} In 303 NBA games (117 starts), Griffin averaged 7.2 points, 5.8 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 1.7 blocks, and 22:12 of floor time per game. ==Death== Griffin died as a result of a car crash on August 17, 2007, at approximately 1:30 a.m. Houston police said in a report that Griffin ignored a railroad warning and went through a barrier before striking a moving train. The resulting fire burned Griffin's SUV and the side of a railcar carrying plastic granules.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2985307 |title=Griffin killed when car hit train last week |publisher=ESPN |date=August 22, 2007}} Griffin's body was badly burned and there was no initial identification. Dental records later revealed the man was Griffin. He had more than three times the legal alcohol limit in his system when he crashed, according to an [[autopsy]] report. The Harris County Medical Examiner's office said the 25-year-old Griffin died of "multiple blunt force injuries." The medical examiner's office performed tests on Griffin's bile and blood from his heart and liver and determined his blood-alcohol level was 0.26; the legal limit in Texas is 0.08. Tests found no traces of cocaine, barbiturates or any other narcotics.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3081412|title= Autopsy shows Griffin had more than 3 times blood-alcohol limit |publisher=ESPN |date=October 26, 2007|access-date=February 26, 2020}} Former Timberwolves coach [[Dwane Casey]] said he had not talked to Griffin in five or six months, but he knew that Griffin was spending the summer trying to get back in shape to play in Europe the next season.{{cite web |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/nba/story/7142852 |title= Griffin killed in SUV collision with train|work=Fox Sports |access-date=2012-01-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070824135229/http://msn.foxsports.com/nba/story/7142852 |archive-date=2007-08-24 }} He was buried in [[Northwood Cemetery]] in Philadelphia.[http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/philly/obituary.aspx?n=eddie-j-griffin&pid=93384684&fhid=4037 Philly.com via Legacy] At the time of his death he had a three-year-old daughter named Amaree.[http://www.thebulletin.us/site/news.cfm?newsid=18759201&BRD=2737&PAG=461&dept_id=576361&rfi=6 Griffin's Funeral Brings Together Those Who Knew 'A Great Kid']
